sections.markdown:
## C — Road-test vehicle rules, vehicle insurance minimums, the National Driver Register, Arizona residency, voter registration, organ donation and the medical indicator
Knowledge domain: the remaining road-test vehicle rules, the liability insurance every Arizona vehicle must carry, the national problem-driver check, who counts as an Arizona resident, and the voter, donor, medical and Social Security choices made on the license application.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
For the road test, the driver and passenger side windows must work and both front doors must open and close properly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
At the road test you must show proof of current registration and current automobile liability insurance for the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
A road test vehicle that is a 1972 model or newer must have seat belts, and they must be fastened and adjusted properly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Advanced Driver Assistance Systems such as auto-drive and parking assistance are banned during the road test, so every maneuver must be done by hand. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Every motor vehicle driven on Arizona roads must be covered by a liability insurance policy from a company licensed to do business in Arizona. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
The policy must be an Arizona-based policy that matches where the vehicle is mainly driven. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
Arizona's minimum liability coverage for a private passenger vehicle is $25,000 for bodily injury to one person, $50,000 for bodily injury to two or more people, and $15,000 for property damage. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
Check that the VIN your insurance company reports matches the VIN on your registration, and ask the insurer to resubmit the correct VIN if it does not. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
You must keep proof of current insurance in the vehicle whenever you drive, because officers ask for it at traffic stops and at crashes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Insurance companies report every new policy, cancellation and non-renewal to MVD, and MVD sends you an inquiry if your insurer says your policy is no longer active. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
Not keeping proper Arizona insurance with a correct VIN on file can lead MVD to suspend your vehicle registration, your driver license, or both. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
You can confirm the insurance MVD has on file by using the Manage Insurance option at AZMVDNow.gov. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A01
Arizona belongs to the National Driver Register, a nationwide computer system about problem drivers, and every Arizona license application is checked against it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A01
If the register shows outstanding or unresolved actions against you in another state, Arizona will not issue you a license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A01
Giving false information on your application can get your Arizona license canceled. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
State law requires you to get an Arizona driver license and vehicle registration right away once any one of the listed residency conditions applies to you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
Those conditions include working in Arizona (seasonal farm work excepted) and enrolling children in school without paying the non-resident tuition rate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
They also include having a business office in Arizona that bases and operates vehicles here, or running a business that moves goods or passengers within Arizona. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
Getting a state license or paying school tuition at the resident rate also makes you a resident for licensing purposes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
Staying in Arizona for seven months or more in total during any calendar year makes you a resident no matter where your permanent home is. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
Being registered to vote in Arizona is another condition that triggers the duty to get an Arizona license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
An out-of-state student taking seven or more semester hours is not considered an Arizona resident, even with a job in the state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
The driver license or ID application includes a voter registration portion you can fill out at the same time, but registering is not required to get a license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
If you decline to register to vote, that choice stays confidential, and if you do register, the application is kept confidential and used only for voter registration. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A02
Submitting a false voter registration is a Class 6 felony in Arizona. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A02
To register to vote you must be at least 18 by the next General Election, a United States citizen and an Arizona resident. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A02
You also cannot have a felony conviction unless your civil rights were restored, and you cannot have been adjudicated incompetent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
Besides the license application, you can register to vote online at AZMVDNow.gov or on a separate form available at MVD offices. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A03
To vote in an upcoming election you must be registered 29 days before it, and registering costs nothing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A03
When you change your address you must register to vote again. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A03
The license or ID application has a box to join the Donate Life AZ Registry as an organ and tissue donor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A03
You can also sign up as a donor by saying yes at an MVD or third-party office, by checking the box when applying online at AZMVDNow.gov, or through DonateLifeAZ.org. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A03
Your license has space for a medical condition indicator for conditions that may need immediate attention. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A03
Getting the medical code takes paperwork about the condition: a statement signed by a licensed physician or by a registered nurse practitioner, or an advanced healthcare directive. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A03
State and federal law require you to provide proof of a valid Social Security number when you apply. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0011]

Misconceptions: carrying insurance is not enough if the VIN on file is wrong — a mismatch can still lead to suspension; registering to vote is offered with the license but is never required; an out-of-state student with a job here is still not a resident; driver-assist features cannot be used to pass the road test.
Mnemonics: for liability minimums remember twenty-five, fifty, fifteen — one person, two or more people, property; for residency, think Work, School, Business, Seven months, Vote.
Glossary: liability insurance means coverage that pays for injuries or damage you cause to others; National Driver Register means the nationwide database of problem drivers checked on every application; ADAS means Advanced Driver Assistance Systems such as auto-drive and parking assistance; medical condition indicator means a code on the license flagging a condition that may need immediate attention.
Dynamic facts: voter-registration contact numbers, the donor registry sign-up channels and online service names can change and are kept out of stable knowledge; insurance minimums come from statute and change only by law.
